newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat trade thin, prices steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: German wheat trade thin, prices steady to lower.

text.p: German wheat export prices are easing along with other European origins as improved crop weather boosts supply prospects for the 1997 harvest, brokers said on Wednesday.
But the northern German grain exchange in Hamburg kept its nominal weekly prices steady to reflect tight old crop supply and underlying European milling industry demand.
Trading was thin ahead of a public holiday on Thursday.

The European Union decision to tax wheat exports had put pressure on prices, but German wheat should remain relatively firm on demand both in the run-up to the new crop and in the 1997/98 season, traders said.
The Hamburg grain exchange quoted wheat (12.5 percent, 220 Hagberg) at 287.50 marks a tonne free Hamburg.
It left the spot feed wheat price unchanged at 280.
Fob Baltic sellers dropped nominal first half May delivery wheat by between 1.00 and 2.50 marks.
They quoted 12 percent protein wheat at 287.50-300 marks and material with 13/14 percent protein at 292.50-319 marks.
Fob Baltic barley and rye offers were unchanged at 273.50 marks spot and at 270-275 marks respectively.
Prices held steady because domestic supplies were extremely thin. Millers were still looking for bread rye.
New crop wheat fob Baltic was offered in a 285-305 marks range and fob Rostock at 292.50-315, depending on dates, quality and shipment sizes.
Buyers were not forthcoming after some initial trade house hedge purchases, brokers said.
